title: Quantization-aware attention kernel router and memory fragmentation compactor
creator: Asha Patel
description: Background: Recent integration of FlashAttention v3 quantized kernels into the runtime improved throughput for many workloads but exposed sporadic decode latency regressions and OOMs on long-prefill workloads when GPU workspace memory became fragmented. Root cause analysis points to two interacting issues: (1) certain v3 quant kernels have a wider transient workspace variance versus v2 kernels depending on microtiling and head-slicing choices, and (2) runtime workspace allocation patterns (malloc/free bursts and KV cache retention) lead to fragmentation and failed allocations for prefill. Scope: Implement a quantization-aware kernel router that factors in (a) model quantization profile (fp16/int8/quantized-fused), (b) recent workspace fragmentation metric, and (c) prefill vs decode phase, to select a kernel variant safely. Also implement a lightweight in-process memory compactor/shim that reduces fragmentation by trimming cached temporary allocations, deferring large KV cache pinning during prefill, and optionally triggering cudaMallocAsync trimming/sync heuristics on fragmentation thresholds. Deliverables: router config API, fragmentation metrics and dashboards, compactor implementation behind a runtime flag, canary rollout plan and rollback hooks, test harness and microbench results.
acceptance_criteria: Router correctly picks v3 quant kernels when model profile indicates low workspace variance and fragmentation metric < 12%
Failover to v2 (or non-quant fallback) occurs deterministically when fragmentation >= 12% or when prefill latency p99 increases > 3% in synthetic harness
Memory compactor reduces observed fragmentation metric by at least 30% in worst-case lab repro and prevents OOMs on the repro cluster
End-to-end canary shows no more than 2% p99 latency regression versus baseline for seq256 workloads and no OOMs for seq1024 prefill across two GPU families (A100, H100)
Documentation update and runtime config knobs present in Console (routing-policy, fragmentation-threshold, compactor-enabled)

notes: 2026-02-21: Initial profiling shows v3 int8 kernel transient workspace peaks up to 1.9x vs v2 for head-slicing=16 on A100 (seq1024 prefill).
2026-02-25: Reproduced OOM on repro cluster when mixing quant v3 kernels with heavy KV cache retention; OOM occurs during prefill allocation attempt for attention workspace.
2026-03-02: POC router returns to v2 for prefill when fragmentation gauge > 12% and keeps v3 for decode; early lab runs show p50 speedups preserved, p99 regressions mitigated.

2026-03-05: Memory compactor POC (truncate temp pool + cudaMallocAsync sync) reduced fragmentation metric by ~38% on repro node but added ~1.2ms mean allocation overhead on some paths. Trade-off documented.
2026-03-08: Design review with PM/DS concluded: expose fragmentation threshold as tuning knob, default conservative behavior to preserve reliability for P1 customers.
